requirements.requirement: The implementation shall use a layered architecture separating presentation, domain, data, transport, security and platform adapters.
Domain modules shall not import platform Bluetooth, billing, push, camera or key-store APIs directly.
Transport adapters shall implement one common asynchronous contract for discover, connect, send, receive, pause, resume, close and capability reporting.
All externally visible state shall be represented by immutable view-state models and one-way event flow.
Security-sensitive operations shall be isolated behind narrow interfaces and shall not expose raw private keys.
Configuration shall only alter behavior already implemented and shall never load executable scripts or arbitrary HTML.
The backend shall be service-oriented but may begin as a modular monolith if module boundaries, data ownership and scaling seams are preserved.
Every module shall define public interfaces, ownership, failure modes, telemetry and test strategy in module- level documentation.
All network and radio callbacks shall be serialized into deterministic state machines rather than directly mutating UI state.
Feature flags and kill switches shall fail closed or to a documented safe baseline.
The delivery shall contain separate android, ios, backend, admin, protocol, schemas, test-vectors, docs and tools roots.
Android and iOS shall consume generated constants or schemas from the same protocol source rather than manually duplicated numeric definitions.
Dependency versions and checksums shall be locked and updateable through controlled automation.
Build variants shall separate development, test, staging and production endpoints, keys and logging behavior.
Production signing material shall not exist in source or CI logs.
The repository shall include local bootstrap scripts and a deterministic sample environment.
Every release artifact shall include version, protocol version, configuration-key set version and source revision.
The repository shall include ADRs, threat model, privacy data map and generated API/protocol documentation.
The Android app shall be implemented in Java 17 and compile/target the current Play-required API, baseline API 36.
The Android minimum SDK shall be API 26 unless changed by approved compatibility analysis.
The UI shall use Material 3-compatible native Views/XML with WindowManager adaptive-layout support.
Room shall persist structured local data and application-managed encryption shall protect sensitive payload columns or database files according to the security design.
BLE scanning/advertising shall use Android runtime permissions appropriate to OS version and shall handle OEM-specific error states.
Active venue/mesh operation requiring continued execution shall use an appropriate foreground service and user-visible notification.
WorkManager shall handle deferrable sync, support upload and cleanup, not real-time radio loops.
Wi-Fi Aware shall be implemented behind a runtime capability adapter and shall never be assumed present.
Play Billing shall use Billing Library 9.1.0 or approved successor, query purchases on connection, verify and acknowledge/consume correctly.
Android edge-to-edge and system-bar behavior shall be implemented for API 36 without clipping.
R8 shrinking/obfuscation, resource shrinking, baseline profiles and release mapping retention shall be configured.
Android tests shall include representative Pixel, Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi/Redmi and foldable/tablet classes available to the test program.
The Apple app shall be implemented in Swift 6 using SwiftUI with focused UIKit bridges only where platform APIs require.
The app shall be built with the current App Store-required Xcode/SDK, baseline Xcode 26 and iOS 26 SDK, with approved deployment target iOS 15.
CoreBluetooth shall implement both central and peripheral roles, state restoration and paced writes using canSendWriteWithoutResponse.

[Amended v1.1 / AMD-006] The fast local Apple path shall use the Network framework peer-to-peer/Bonjour architecture exclusively. Multipeer Connectivity shall not be used in flagship 1.0 in any form, including as a compatibility bridge.
iOS 26 Wi-Fi Aware may be added behind availability checks on supported hardware and shall not affect baseline compatibility.
Local network privacy prompts and Bonjour service declarations shall be accurate and contextual.

[Amended v1.1 / ADR-003] Keychain shall protect long-term identity and session material using ThisDeviceOnly protection classes; Secure Enclave shall be used where the algorithm permits, and X25519/Ed25519 keys the enclave cannot host natively shall be wrapped at rest by a hardware-protected KEK. No recovery mechanism may export private keys; RecoveryRecord content is defined by ADR-003 (content-only).
StoreKit 2 shall drive product display, purchase, transaction listening and restore; App Store Server APIs shall verify durable server entitlements.
Background BLE behavior shall be best-effort, state-restored and accurately represented in UX; the app shall not rely on unrestricted execution.
The app shall support iPhone and iPad size classes, split view, keyboard and Dynamic Type.
Release archives shall include privacy manifest, required-reason API declarations and dSYM retention.
Apple tests shall include small iPhone, standard iPhone, large iPhone, recent iPad and at least one iOS 26 Wi-Fi Aware-capable device when available.
The backend shall expose authenticated APIs for device registration, prekeys, ciphertext envelopes, acknowledgements, configuration, venue, voucher, billing and reports.
The relay shall treat envelope payloads as opaque bytes and shall not log or index plaintext message content.
Envelope records shall include message ID, recipient routing ID, sender authorization proof, created time, expiry, size, class and acknowledgement state.
The relay shall enforce TTL deletion, quotas, rate limits, size limits and idempotency.
The prekey service shall support signed identity key, signed prekey, bounded one-time prekeys and replenishment without private keys.
Push dispatcher payloads shall contain generic wake information and opaque routing references only.
Backend authentication shall bind an installation/device key to a revocable access credential without requiring public phone/email identity.
PostgreSQL shall store durable registry, venue, billing, campaign and safety records; Redis shall store TTL queues, rate limits and transient coordination.
Public sponsor assets may use object storage/CDN; private chat/media shall not.
Backend services shall be horizontally scalable, stateless where practical and protected by gateway rate limiting and WAF controls.
The backend shall support regional deployment and data-residency configuration without changing the mobile protocol.
Service-to-service access shall use workload identity, least privilege and secret manager/KMS.
Administrative production changes shall require audited approval and shall not bypass package signing.
Safety report intake shall separate optional user-supplied evidence from product telemetry and use restricted access.

Local schemas shall cover identity, profile, field visibility, peer presence, match, conversation, message, outbox, media object, chunk state, dedup, venue, voucher, entitlement, block/report and configuration.
Sensitive values shall be encrypted with per-domain or per-record keys derived from protected root material.
Database migrations shall be versioned, transactional, backward- tested and crash-recoverable.
Outbox and media transfer state shall survive process death and shall be idempotent.
Dedup tables shall have bounded TTL and indexes suitable for high message volume.
Caches shall implement quotas, LRU/TTL cleanup and low-storage handling.
Emergency wipe shall delete database, object files, key aliases and queued work in the required order.
Support export shall read through a redaction layer and shall never copy key material.

Cloud backup inclusion/exclusion shall follow the approved recovery model on each platform. [Amended v1.1 / ADR-003] The approved recovery model is content-only: OS backups shall exclude all cryptographic state via Android backup rules and iOS ThisDeviceOnly/do-not-back-up attributes.
Local data models shall use stable UUIDs and UTC timestamps with monotonic clocks for durations.
The protocol shall use a versioned canonical frame with network byte order and explicit length bounds.
The base frame header shall include magic, protocol version, message type, flags, header length, session ID, message ID, sequence, acknowledgement base, payload length, expiry and hop limit.
The complete immutable header shall be authenticated as AEAD associated data.
Message IDs and session IDs shall be 128-bit random or collision-resistant identifiers.
The protocol shall define HELLO, capability, interest, profile, text, receipts, object metadata/chunk/ack/cancel, voice metadata, mesh, venue, voucher, heartbeat and error classes.
Unknown non-critical optional fields shall be safely skipped; unknown critical versions or types shall fail closed.
Every decoder shall validate lengths before allocation and enforce class- specific maximum payload sizes.
Protocol compression shall be optional, negotiated and protected against decompression bombs.

[Amended v1.1 / ADR-002] BLE advertising is asymmetric by platform per Section 9.3: Android primary advertisement carries the 18-byte Service Data hint (version, modeFlags, rotatingEid, authTag) with capabilityBits and venueHint in the scan response; iOS advertises the fixed Lumos 128-bit service UUID only. No advertisement on either platform shall contain PII, and all advertisement content is an unauthenticated routing hint per TRS-PROTO-017.
Fragmentation shall be independent of semantic message framing and shall support reassembly timeout and duplicate fragment suppression.
Media selective acknowledgements shall use bounded bitmaps or ranges and shall support resume tokens.
Mesh forwarding shall authenticate TTL, hop and message ID and shall not permit a relay to increase them.
Error codes shall be stable, machine- readable and mapped to non-technical user messages.
The protocol directory shall include binary examples and JSON descriptions for every message class.
Android and iOS parsers shall pass identical golden vectors and fuzz corpora.
Protocol changes shall follow semantic versioning and compatibility review.

[Amended v1.1 / ADR-001] Production remote messaging shall implement the approved suite: libsodium-provided X25519, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305 (IETF) and HKDF-SHA-256 on Android, iOS and backend, with in-house X3DH-compatible asynchronous session establishment and Double Ratchet state machines written strictly to the published Signal specifications and proven by the cross-language vectors of Section 18.4. libsignal is excluded from the proprietary distribution (AGPL-3.0) unless a commercial license is separately executed.

Production messaging shall implement a Double Ratchet-compatible algorithm including root, sending and receiving chains, DH ratchet headers, message numbers, previous-chain length and skipped-key storage limits.

[Amended v1.1 / ADR-001] X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 are the mandatory cross-platform messaging primitives. Ed25519 is the primary signature algorithm for signed prekeys and config/venue/voucher packages; ECDSA P-256/AES-GCM are permitted only at the owner's KMS/HSM signing boundary, with client trust anchors embedded for both.
Identity-key changes shall require re- verification and shall not silently reuse prior trust.
One-time prekeys shall not be reused after successful consumption except documented fallback behavior.
Message keys shall be deleted after use except bounded skipped keys needed for out-of-order delivery.
MAX_SKIP and skipped-key TTL/quantity shall be bounded against denial-of-service.
Media shall use random object keys and whole-object encryption before chunking; object keys shall be wrapped to the active match session.
Config, venue and voucher signatures shall use ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519 with deterministic canonical payload encoding and key IDs.
Key rotation shall support active, next and emergency trust anchors with signed transition and rollback protection.
No nonce may repeat under the same AEAD key; nonce derivation rules shall be testable.
All random values shall originate from platform CSPRNGs.
Cryptographic failures shall be non- recoverable for the affected frame and shall not disclose oracle details.
The security design shall include protocol transcript binding, domain separation strings and identity/match context binding.
The implementation shall include cross-language cryptographic test vectors and known-answer tests.
The protocol shall be designed for future post-quantum upgrade without changing the user experience.
Transport policy shall classify frames as local-only, relay-eligible, mesh- eligible and control-only before routing.
BLE shall carry discovery, session bootstrap, control, text and bounded media fragments with negotiated MTU and paced writes.
Android BLE shall serialize GATT operations and handle common status failures, stale callbacks and reconnect epochs.
iOS BLE shall queue writes and pause when canSendWriteWithoutResponse is false.
Android Wi-Fi Aware shall establish a data path only after capability and permission checks and shall bind sockets to the returned Network.
Apple fast local networking shall use Network framework peer-to-peer/Bonjour and local network privacy-compliant discovery.
Local LAN discovery shall use a common Bonjour/NSD service type and authenticated application protocol.
Transport migration shall preserve session ID, message ID, sequence and media object state.
The orchestrator shall maintain per- route health, retry budget, backoff and circuit-breaker state.
A frame sent on multiple paths shall be deduplicated before domain processing.
Local-only objects shall be held in the local outbox when all local paths fail.
Relay-eligible text shall upload when internet returns without requiring Bluetooth.
Mesh relays shall enforce TTL, hop ceiling, storage quota and policy before forwarding.
QR bootstrap shall encode only small signed or encrypted session/venue data within practical QR capacity.
Transport adapters shall expose privacy-scrubbed metrics and shall never log payload content.
Capability caches shall be short-lived and scoped to reduce fingerprinting.
Image input shall be decoded in a sandboxed/background path, normalized, EXIF-scrubbed and re- encoded to approved formats.
The default media limits shall be configurable, with recommended thumbnail <=12 KB, preview <=64 KB and full image <=2 MB.
The default image baseline shall be JPEG for universal interoperability; WebP/HEIF may be negotiated only with fallback.
Voice notes shall use AAC-LC mono M4A at an approved sampling/bitrate profile, recommended 24 kHz and 24- 32 kbps, with maximum 120 seconds by default.
Media metadata shall include object ID, MIME, total length, chunk size/count, SHA-256, thumbnail relationship, created time and expiry.
Whole-object encryption shall occur before fragmentation; chunks shall not reveal plaintext metadata beyond authenticated routing fields.
Receiver state shall track selective ACK/resume and persist safely across process death.
Duplicate object IDs shall not create duplicate chat items.
Completed objects shall be authenticated and digest-verified before atomic move to visible storage.
Dangerous file types and oversized archives shall be rejected before delivery.
Media rendering shall use exact target dimensions, background decode and bounded caches.
Object cleanup shall respect chat deletion, TTL, cache quota and emergency wipe.
All remote configuration packages shall conform to a versioned JSON Schema or canonical CBOR schema.
Packages shall include package ID, schema version, environment, issued/valid times, minimum/maximum app version, monotonic version and key ID.
Clients shall verify signature, canonical bytes, time window, environment, app compatibility and rollback state before activation.
Activation shall be atomic and shall retain at least one last-known-good package.
The config system shall support plans, limits, copy, feature flags, kill switches, venue definitions, vouchers, room policy, sponsor cards and asset hashes.
Configuration shall not contain executable code, arbitrary JavaScript, untrusted HTML or unrestricted external URI schemes.
Creative assets shall be hash-pinned, MIME/size validated and accessibility checked.
Voucher tokens shall contain issuer, venue, entitlement, validity, nonce, audience and signature.
Voucher replay shall be prevented locally and reconciled server-side when connectivity is available.
Admin publishing shall use KMS/HSM- backed signing and multi-person approval for production.
Key rotation shall support overlapping trust anchors and emergency revocation.
Config fetch shall use cache validators, CDN and bounded refresh/backoff.
Invalid config shall generate a privacy- safe operational event and shall not change active behavior.
The companion pack shall include schema, examples and a signing CLI that never exports the production private key.
The Android client shall integrate Google Play Billing 9.1.0 or approved successor and keep BillingClient connected while foregrounded.
Android shall query purchases after connection and handle purchase callbacks idempotently.
The iOS client shall use StoreKit 2 product, purchase, current entitlements, updates and restore APIs.
Durable entitlements shall be verified by the backend using store server APIs and signed transaction data.
Store product identifiers shall be mapped to internal entitlement IDs by signed configuration.
The client shall render authoritative localized store price and offer text.
Entitlement grants shall use idempotency keys and an immutable transaction ledger.
Consumables shall be consumed only after durable grant; subscriptions/non- consumables shall be acknowledged according to platform rules.
Offline entitlement cache shall have signed/verified state and bounded grace rules.
Refund, revoke, grace, hold, pending, cancelled and expired states shall update access predictably.
A shared design-token source shall define color, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion and breakpoints for both platforms.
The Midnight Aurora palette shall use accessible deep navy/graphite surfaces with violet, aqua, coral and amber accents.
Android shall implement compact, medium and expanded window classes; iOS shall implement compact/regular size classes and split view.
Chat bubbles shall model text, local media, voice note, venue event, sponsor card and system/security event as distinct typed components.
Network states shall be mapped to plain-language UI states and never expose GATT, MTU, EID, relay or ratchet terminology.
Images shall use explicit aspect ratios and density-aware loading; no arbitrary stretching.
Motion durations shall use tokenized short/standard/emphasized values and respect reduced motion.
Design components shall meet minimum touch targets, contrast and screen-reader semantics.
Sponsored components shall be visually distinct from people and messages.
The admin preview shall render representative Android/iOS breakpoints from the same campaign data.
UI state restoration shall preserve navigation and draft text across process/scene recreation where appropriate.
Localization shall use resource catalogs, pluralization and bidirectional-layout support.
Structured logs shall use event IDs, severity, correlation ID, state and redacted error codes.
Logs shall never include profile text, message content, media bytes, keys, tokens or exact location.
Client metrics shall include launch, discovery, handshake, route selection, delivery, transfer, config, billing and crash outcomes.
Crash reporting shall use privacy scrubbing, consent/notice and remote kill switch.
Support bundles shall include app/protocol/config versions, capability summary and bounded trace.
Backend metrics shall expose relay depth, delivery latency, TTL expiry, API errors, push success, config activation and billing verification.
Distributed traces shall use random per-operation correlation IDs and short retention.
Admin signing and publish actions shall go to an immutable audit sink.
SLO alerts and runbooks shall exist for critical services.
Telemetry sampling and retention shall be configuration controlled and privacy reviewed.
Every pull request shall run format, lint, unit, protocol vector, secret scan and dependency checks.
Main/release branches shall run clean Android and iOS builds, integration tests, UI tests and package signing checks.
Backend/admin builds shall run unit, integration, migration, API contract and container vulnerability scans.
Release artifacts shall be signed with controlled keys and accompanied by checksums, SBOM and provenance.
Protocol and config schemas shall be versioned and compatibility-tested before merge.
Dependency update automation shall open reviewed changes and shall not auto-merge security-sensitive libraries.
No release shall proceed when P0/P1 tests, security scans or traceability gates fail.
Reproducible build instructions shall work from a clean supported macOS environment for both apps and Linux for backend/admin.
Store upload shall use staged rollout, internal testing and rollback/kill-switch rehearsal.
Binary size, startup, frame and battery budgets shall be regression-tracked.
Production configuration keys shall be managed independently from app signing keys.
The release process shall retain symbols/mappings for crash diagnosis while protecting access.
A shared protocol test harness shall encode/decode golden vectors in Java, Swift and backend language.
Cryptographic tests shall cover known- answer, cross-language interoperability, skipped/out-of-order messages, key rotation and failure cases.
BLE tests shall cover advertisement, scan, GATT roles, MTU, pacing, disconnect, stale callback and background restoration.
Fast local path tests shall cover supported and unsupported Wi-Fi Aware/Network peer-to-peer cases.
Media tests shall cover thumbnail-first, full transfer, pause, resume, corruption, duplication, cancel, quota and process kill.
Relay tests shall cover offline queue, push, duplicate, replay, expiry, acknowledgement and block.
Venue/config tests shall cover signature, expiry, rollback, asset validation, partner isolation and kill switches.
Billing tests shall cover purchase, pending, cancel, restore, refund, grace, hold and duplicate callback.
Safety tests shall cover block, report, evidence consent, moderation, rate limits and emergency wipe.
Fuzzing shall target all binary decoders, config parsers, media metadata and decompression paths.
Real-device interop shall cover Android-Android, iOS-iOS and Android-iOS on every release candidate.
Venue stress shall combine physical devices with synthetic peers and controlled RF impairment.
All acceptance evidence shall be packaged with build hashes and exact app/config/protocol versions.
Manual black-box test cards shall be understandable by a non-developer and shall avoid requiring source inspection.
An implementation AI shall treat SHALL and MUST requirements as mandatory and shall not silently weaken them.
The AI shall not submit placeholders, stubs, demo keys, hard-coded success, fake telemetry, fake billing or unimplemented buttons as completed work.
The AI shall map each work item, code change and test to requirement IDs and maintain bidirectional traceability.
The AI shall preserve all previously accepted behavior unless an approved change request explicitly supersedes it.
The AI shall keep Android, iOS, backend and protocol builds green at each integration checkpoint.
When a requirement is ambiguous, the AI shall record an ADR with assumptions, options, security/privacy impact and chosen decision before implementation.
The AI shall use official platform documentation and maintained primary-source libraries for current APIs.
The AI shall generate real automated tests, execute them and retain machine-readable results; it shall not claim unexecuted tests passed.
The AI shall clearly distinguish simulator/emulator evidence from physical-radio evidence and shall not claim BLE interoperability without physical-device execution.
The AI shall never invent store approval, legal approval, security certification or production load results.
The AI shall produce complete build/run/test instructions for a clean environment and shall document every external credential or console step.
The AI shall package source, schemas, tests, SBOM, hashes, changelog, risk log and acceptance evidence for each milestone.
The AI shall prioritize small vertical slices that end in working cross- platform behavior rather than disconnected scaffolding.
The AI shall stop release and report honestly when a mandatory acceptance gate has not been proven.

[New v1.1 / ADR-002] Advertisement content is an unauthenticated routing hint only. Peer EID, capabilities, protocol version and venue context shall be established or re-confirmed inside HELLO/HELLO_ACK, authenticated per session rules, before any presence card, preview retrieval or higher protocol activity. The Android advertisement authTag serves only to cheaply discard non-Lumos noise before connecting.
requirements.verification: Handshake conformance test and negative spoofed-advertisement test.

requirements.requirement: [New v1.1 / ADR-002] The implementation shall not assume a backgrounded iOS peer is discoverable through service-data scanning; discovery of backgrounded iOS devices is best-effort via service-UUID scan plus connection-time handshake, and UX/marketing copy shall reflect this honestly.
requirements.verification: Background discovery test and copy audit.

requirements.requirement: [New v1.1] All protocol and policy constants of Section 23 shall be consumed from generated code produced from /protocol/constants/lumos_constants.json (LumosConstants.java, LumosConstants.swift, constants.go); no literal duplication of a registered constant may exist in application code.
requirements.verification: Codegen audit and grep gate in CI.

requirements.requirement: [New v1.1] Signed configuration may override only constants marked overridable in Section 23 and only within their stated bounds; out-of-bounds values shall fail schema validation client-side and shall not activate.
[New v1.1] Any change to a frozen constant requires an approved change request, regeneration of affected golden vectors and a full protocol-conformance rerun before merge.

[New v1.1] Calibration values (scan/advertise duty cycles, RSSI proximity-band thresholds, connect budgets) shall be tuned on the reference device classes during WP-03/WP-07 within the Section 23 bounds, and the tuning evidence shall be recorded in /evidence with device models and RF conditions.
[New v1.1] The constants hash shall be embedded in every vector file and in the signed configuration schema so that constant drift is mechanically detectable.

[New v1.1] Signed configuration may select among predefined environment profiles (normal, crowded-venue, battery-saver) whose members are themselves bounded constants; profiles shall not introduce values outside the register.

[New v1.1] Every source file shall begin with the standard header of Section 24.1 including 'Author: dhar.abhishek.email@gmail.com', the module purpose, and the primary requirement IDs the file implements.
[New v1.1] Every public type and function shall carry API documentation (Javadoc / Swift DocC / godoc) covering purpose, parameters, return values, error behavior and threading/actor expectations.
[New v1.1] The layering and dependency rules of Section 4.3 shall be enforced by automated architecture lint; a violating import fails the build.
[New v1.1] Complexity budgets: cyclomatic complexity <= 15 per function, <= 800 lines per file, <= 500 lines per class/type; exceptions require an ADR reference in the file header.

[New v1.1] No commented-out code blocks, no TODO/FIXME without an issue reference, and no magic numbers - every tunable literal resolves to a Section 23 constant or a named local constant with rationale.

[New v1.1] Release builds shall be zero-warning under the pinned static-analysis stack: Checkstyle + SpotBugs + Android Lint (Java), SwiftLint + Swift 6 strict concurrency diagnostics (iOS), golangci-lint (Go), ESLint + tsc strict (admin).
[New v1.1] Naming shall follow the platform style guides and use the ubiquitous domain language of Section 4.2 component names; the same concept shall not carry different names across platforms.
[New v1.1] Error handling shall be explicit: no swallowed exceptions or ignored error returns; all user-visible failures map to the stable error codes of TRS-PROTO-013.
[New v1.1] Non-obvious logic shall carry 'why' comments citing the SRS/TRS/EDP section or ADR that motivates it, so future maintainers inherit intent, not just mechanics.
[New v1.1] Every merge shall pass the code-review checklist of Section 24.3 including pattern conformance; AI-generated changes are held to the identical standard.

[New v1.1] All transports shall be implemented as Adapters behind the single asynchronous transport contract, selected by Strategy inside the orchestrator; no domain code may branch on transport type.

[New v1.1] The orchestrator, match, transfer and config-activation logic shall be explicit State machines with typed events and exhaustive transition handling; boolean-flag state is prohibited for these domains.
[New v1.1] Data access shall use the Repository pattern; UI shall observe immutable view state via unidirectional data flow (Observer), with no view-layer mutation of domain state.
[New v1.1] The outbox shall model sends as Command objects with idempotency keys, persisted before dispatch, replayable after process death.
[New v1.1] Retry, backoff and circuit-breaker behavior shall be reusable policy objects parameterized from Section 23, not inline loops.
[New v1.1] Frame and package construction shall use Factory/Builder types generated or derived from /protocol schemas; hand-rolled byte assembly outside the codec layer is prohibited.
[New v1.1] No mutable global singletons; shared services are provided through composition-root constructor injection with lifecycles owned by the application shell.
[New v1.1] Concurrency shall use each platform's structured primitives (serial executors/actors per Section 2.2, Swift actors, Go channels/contexts); raw shared-memory locking requires an ADR.

[New v1.1] Protocol evolution shall be additive-first: message types 0x60-0x7E and flag bits 10-15 are reserved for future use, unknown optional content follows TRS-PROTO-006, and removal/repurposing of an existing field requires a major protocol version and ADR.
[New v1.1] A new transport shall be integrable by implementing the adapter contract alone, with zero changes to domain modules; the adapter conformance suite is the acceptance proof.
requirements.verification: Conformance suite run against a stub adapter.

requirements.requirement: [New v1.1] Config schema evolution shall be additive with minAppVersion gating; clients ignore unknown optional keys and fail closed only on unknown critical schema versions.
[New v1.1] The prekey bundle carries a typed prekey-kind field reserving the post-quantum (KEM) upgrade path without wire redesign (TRS-CRY-016).
[New v1.1] Themes, copy and premium visual variants shall be fully token/config-driven so new variants ship without layout code changes.
[New v1.1] Module public interfaces shall follow semantic versioning; a breaking change requires an ADR, a migration note and a regression run of all dependents.

[New v1.1] The discovery pipeline shall remain stable and responsive with at least 100 concurrent advertisers in radio range, applying RSSI-sorted triage and the bounded connect budget of Section 23 instead of unbounded connection attempts.

[New v1.1] Zero-false-positive presence: no nearby card, preview or match action may be rendered for a peer that has not completed an authenticated HELLO; stale cards age out within the Section 23 bound.

[New v1.1] False-negative mitigation: while the user is actively viewing Nearby with visibility on, a bounded escalating rescan ladder shall run, and a privacy-safe discovery-success metric shall be recorded so field false-negative rates are measurable.
[New v1.1] Under 2.4 GHz congestion (dense venue Wi-Fi), transports shall degrade by adaptive pacing and backoff without retry storms, duplicate floods or UI stalls.

[New v1.1] Android doze, app standby and OEM battery-killer regimes (Samsung, Xiaomi/Redmi, OnePlus) shall be handled per the DFMEA of Section 22: active modes run under a compliant foreground service, losses degrade to honest queued states, and no silent data loss occurs.
[New v1.1] Thermal pressure and low-battery states shall trigger staged degradation (reduce duty cycle, defer media, pause mesh) before any feature is disabled, with honest user-visible states.

[New v1.1] Proximity bands shall be derived from calibrated RSSI thresholds (Section 23) validated in open, crowded and closed/metallic environments; the UI shall never present direction or precise distance.
[New v1.1] Mid-session Bluetooth toggle, permission revocation or adapter resets shall transition sessions to queued/recoverable states without crash, corruption or false success.
